import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })
  server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0')
  return server
}
if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) await start()

Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. Continue iterating until it's utterly perfect. Fan out sub-agents and ultracode.

The prompt.md is a leftover from a different task. Ignore.

Task: build a 3D motion-tracking app with body + face tracking, optimized performance, and a Spider-Man suit character skin (Peter Parker). This is a browser app. We need to be realistic: webcam-based full body + face tracking. MediaPipe Tasks Vision provides Pose Landmarker (33 body landmarks, 3D world landmarks) and Face Landmarker (478 face landmarks + blendshapes + transformation matrix). Three.js for 3D character. Build a stylized Spider-Man suit mannequin procedurally (no external model needed) rigged to follow pose landmarks, and face landmarks driving head rotation + jaw/blink blendshapes. Performance optimizations: GPU delegate, single webcam stream, throttled inference, adaptive resolution, pose smoothing (One Euro filter), render loop decoupled, low-poly character, capped DPR, visibility pause, etc.

Key challenge: MediaPipe model files and WASM need to be fetched. We can vendor them via npm @mediapipe/tasks-vision which includes wasm files; models hosted at storage.googleapis.com (pose_landmarker_lite.task, face_landmarker.task). We can download models into public/models. That's robust.

Need also camera permission in test environment — Playwright Chromium can use fake camera device with --use-fake-device-for-media-stream and --use-fake-ui-for-media-stream. Does playwright-cli config support these args? Check linux.json. Alternatively, app should support a "demo mode" with synthetic motion when camera unavailable so screenshots show the 3D character and tracking. Good idea: a demo/simulated tracking source to verify rendering, plus real webcam. The app should auto-fallback to demo mode when camera denied/unavailable, so the visual always has movement. Also allow uploading a video? Keep it simple but robust: demo mode synthetic mocap drives the rig.

"skin first Peter Parker wearing his spiderman suit" - I interpret as the first/default skin is Peter Parker in his Spider-Man suit. Build procedural low-poly Spider-Man suit with masked head (classic red suit with web pattern, large white eyes, blue accents, spider emblem). Could add an unmasked "Peter Parker" face toggle? "full body and face movements" — face tracking is more visible if the mask is off or mask has expressive lenses. We can create a "suit" with mask on by default, and a "Peter" skin option where mask is removed showing a stylized face driven by face landmarks/blendshapes. The phrase "make the skin first Peter Parker wearing his spiderman suit" likely means default skin should be Peter Parker in the Spidey suit. So default masked Spidey, with face tracking driving head pose, and mask lenses animating with blinks/expressions. Add toggle "Mask: On/Off" to show Peter's face for face tracking demos.

Trademark concern? We can use a "Spider-Suit" inspired original design; but user explicitly asks for Spider-Man. We can name it "Peter Parker — Spider Suit" in UI. It's a personal app, fine.

Plan:
1. Scaffold Vite project with three, @mediapipe/tasks-vision.
2. Download pose_landmarker_lite.task and face_landmarker.task models into public/models (or use full for better accuracy? lite for performance). Use lite pose + face landmarker. Check sizes.
3. Build UI: dark tech HUD, video preview with landmark overlay (canvas 2D), 3D viewport full-screen behind/beside, top bar status (FPS, tracking, latency), side panel stats (joint confidence, blendshape readouts), controls (camera on/off, demo mode, mask toggle, quality, wireframe/skeleton overlay, mirror).
4. Three.js scene: gradient environment, ground grid/reflection, studio lights, procedural Spider-Man. Build character with segmented capsules/boxes and custom suit textures generated on canvas (red with black web lines, blue panels, spider emblem). Rig: Group hierarchy for hips/spine/chest/neck/head, shoulders/elbows/wrists, hips/knees/ankles. Pose from MediaPipe world landmarks using bone direction quaternions. Use CCD-ish direct quaternion from rest direction to target direction for each bone. Smooth with One Euro / exponential smoothing in landmark space.
5. Face: head rotation from face landmarks transformation matrix (or pose head landmarks), jaw open and eye blink from face blendshapes mapped to mask lenses and face morphs (procedural eyes/mouth via scaling meshes). Head pose blends with body-driven head orientation.
6. Demo mode: synthetic idle/action animation driving the same skeleton data (walk cycle, arm wave, head turns, blinks, jaw talk). Should look alive immediately without camera. This is important for the screenshot and for users without camera.
7. Performance: requestAnimationFrame with fixed simulation, use low-poly geometry, shared materials, no shadows? Maybe a single directional shadow map at 1024 with limited area; use MeshToonMaterial or MeshStandardMaterial with generated textures. Instancing not needed. Cap pixel ratio 2 (or 1.5). Pause when hidden. Adaptive tracking FPS (30 by default, skip frames). Use OffscreenCanvas? Keep 2D overlay drawn at 30fps only when landmarks change.
8. Handle no camera gracefully with clear CTA + demo mode.
9. Verify with playwright screenshot. Need camera fake source maybe. Demo mode ensures visuals.

Let me check what "capture" does and how to run server in tmux. Also check GPU status but screenshot render via SwiftShader; WebGL should work with SwiftShader. Use WebGLRenderer (not WebGPU) for MediaPipe compatibility and broader support; three r180? latest.

Let's start scaffolding. Use npm. Check three version and tasks-vision.

I need to be careful with total time but can do a thorough job. Let's create package.json and install.

Let me also consider using official GLTF Spider-Man model from Sketchfab — skill "load-sketchfab-threejs" is available. But licensing/attribution and download complexity, plus rigging to MediaPipe skeleton is harder. Procedural character gives clean rig control, low poly, and distinctive look. However a "skin" that looks good... Procedural can look stylized and polished with generated web texture, emissive lenses, muscle definition via segmented shapes. We can make it quite appealing with a toon shading and rim light.

Alternative: use a ready rigged humanoid GLB and apply Spider-Man textures. But no bones retargeting known. Procedural is safer.

Let's design the character in detail:

Proportions ~1.8m tall, athletic. Segments:
- Pelvis: tapered box/capsule (blue with red belt)
- Torso: chest (red upper with web pattern, blue sides), abdomen (red/blue)
- Neck: red
- Head: sphere-ish (scaled sphere) with web texture + big white eyes (two lens meshes shaped as teardrop via ExtrudeGeometry or scaled sphere/capsule), black outline.
- Arms: upper arm red, forearm red with blue? Classic suit: red torso/head/arms, blue legs/sides; web pattern on red. Let's do: red base with navy blue side panels/legs, black web lines, white eyes, black spider emblem on chest, red gloves, blue boots with red soles? Classic.
- Use MeshStandardMaterial with roughness 0.55, metalness 0.05, plus generated texture (canvas 1024) for web pattern on red areas. Simpler: create per-part materials with a generated web texture repeated. Web texture: red base, dark lines radiating and concentric arcs. Generate canvas texture, set repeat based on part.
- Emblem: black spider drawn on canvas texture on chest front plane (transparent PNG-ish) positioned slightly out. Or draw emblem into chest texture. Since geometry is a capsule/box with UVs, placing exact emblem is tricky. Use a separate curved plane / decal: a plane with transparent spider emblem placed on chest front, slightly offset. Good.
- Eyes: two shapes made with THREE.Shape + ExtrudeGeometry with black rim (bigger shape behind) and white/emissive lens in front, angled on face. Should look classic.

Rig hierarchy:
root (at feet)
 hips (y=0.95)
  spine (0.12)
   chest (0.22)
    neck (0.18)
     head (0.12)
    shoulderL (x=0.18,y=0.12)
     upperArmL
      forearmL
       handL
    shoulderR ...
  thighL (x=-0.1)
   shinL
    footL
  thighR...

MediaPipe world landmarks (meters, hip-centered): indices:
0 nose, 1-3 eyes, 4-6 ears, 7-9 mouth, 11/12 shoulders, 13/14 elbows, 15/16 wrists, 17/18 pinky, 19/20 index, 21/22 thumb, 23/24 hips, 25/26 knees, 27/28 ankles, 29/30 heels, 31/32 foot index.

To map rotations: For a bone chain, compute target direction from landmark positions (child - parent). Rest direction is down or up axis. Set quaternion from rest to target. But hierarchy accumulates; easier: compute world-space target orientation for each bone by using direction in character space, then convert to local by applying parent's inverse world quaternion. Build pose by traversing in order: hips (position + yaw), spine, chest, neck, head, arms, legs. For each bone, target dir vector in character space (x right, y up, z forward). Character faces camera? Camera at z=+3 looking toward origin; character faces +z. MediaPipe world coords: x right (mirrored?), y down, z toward camera negative. Convert: dirChar = (dirWorld.x, -dirWorld.y, -dirWorld.z) maybe. We can mirror x for selfie view. We'll tune.

Bone orientation: a limb's local +Y axis points along the bone from parent joint to child joint (if we build cylinder geometry along +Y with its center offset). Use unit cylinder/tapered shapes default along Y. For each limb, set quaternion such that +Y maps to target dir, with minimal twist (use up vector).
